transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net customer billing, my name is Darren. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yeah hi Darren, um, I'm ringing because you lot have taken two payments out of my bank account this month and then hit me with a penalty fee, and it's completely wrong.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can look at your billing statement today, Declan. Before I pull up the billing screen, please confirm your billing address and your four digit security PIN.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Address is 85 Belgrave Road, um, Birmingham, B5 7ER, and the PIN is four four one nine.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you Declan, that verifies your account. Your current ledger shows an outstanding balance of ninety-six pounds including a late direct debit fee.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is total nonsense though, you know, my monthly package is only forty-eight pounds, not ninety-six.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The billing record indicates that the direct debit requested on the third of the month was rejected by your banking provider with unpaid return reason code unpaid account closed.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Because I switched bank accounts two weeks ago, um, and I gave S-Net my new bank details online well before the direct debit run! I used the automated Current Account Switch Service.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our automated clearing house BACS payment file was already submitted five full business days prior to the payment date, so the debit was drawn against the legacy closed account number.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Well that is your system's fault, not mine! You tried to pull money from a dead account, charged me two lots of forty-eight pounds plus a twenty-four pound bounce fee, and now my internet has a restriction warning on it! I am absolutely livid about this, it is scandalous!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: To lift the suspension flag from your broadband profile, the full overdue amount of ninety-six pounds needs to be cleared by debit or credit card today.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am not paying ninety-six pounds when you owe me a refund! My new bank details are sort code zero four zero zero zero four and account number eight eight one two three four five six, and that's where the single correct payment should come from.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The system will not allow a direct debit re-submission while an active ledger default is logged against the current statement.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you not manually waive the penalty fee? It was your delay in updating my mandate that caused this whole mess.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Administrative bounce fees are generated automatically by network banking protocols whenever a direct debit instruction fails, and the billing terminal cannot override that debit surcharge prior to account settlement.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is unbelievable. So you make a mistake with my bank details, and I have to pay twenty-four pounds for the privilege? It makes my blood boil.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The terms and conditions of your broadband contract state that direct debit mandate modifications require ten working days to process through the interbank network.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I submitted the mandate online fourteen days ago, um, on the twentieth of last month from my work computer!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Our database timestamp records the mandate submission on the twenty-sixth at four in the afternoon.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Because your website was down for maintenance over the weekend, like I tried three times on the twentieth and it kept giving error five hundred server unavailable!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I do not have access to past web infrastructure server logs from the customer billing queue, Declan, so I can only see the recorded submission date.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can I speak to a supervisor or someone with authority to remove this charge?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: My supervisor would only reiterate the same balance requirement. If you settle forty-eight pounds now, I can temporarily suspend collection on the remainder.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Why should I pay forty-eight pounds now when you already took forty-eight pounds from my credit card as an automated top-up yesterday?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The card payment yesterday was an automated token charge applied when the direct debit returned unpaid.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Exactly! So you HAVE been paid forty-eight pounds! Why does the system say I owe ninety-six then?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The ledger shows the forty-eight pounds card payment is currently in pending unallocated status on the banking gateway.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Well allocate it then! It cleared my bank account yesterday morning.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Pending gateway allocations take up to seventy-two business hours to reconcile against individual account ledgers.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So you have my money sitting in your gateway, but you're still threatening to cut off my broadband unless I pay again?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The restriction will only trigger if the balance remains unresolved after midnight on Friday.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: This is the worst customer service I've ever experienced, honestly.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand you disagree with the ledger timing, Declan. What I can do is raise an official dispute form to our finance audit department.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: How long does that dispute form take to get looked at?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The accounts audit team investigates dispute submissions within five to seven business days and reviews both website error tickets and merchant gateway statements.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And what happens to my internet while they're investigating for a week?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I can place a seven-day temporary hold on the account suspension flag while the audit is pending.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, well please put that seven-day hold on right now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I am applying the seven-day suspension hold code on your broadband profile now.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And what about the twenty-four pound bounce fee? Will that be credited back?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If the audit team verifies that your mandate was submitted prior to the billing freeze date, they will apply a twenty-four pound goodwill credit.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: It shouldn't be a goodwill credit, it should be a complete cancellation of an invalid charge.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That decision rests entirely with the audit team after reviewing the web portal access logs.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: To update the direct debit mandate for next month's payment, what were those new bank account and sort code digits again Declan?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Like I literally just told you ten minutes ago, sort code zero four zero zero zero four and account eight eight one two three four five six! Do you not write anything down?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have to re-enter them into the banking portal directly to ensure zero transcription errors.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Fine. Just make sure it actually saves this time.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The new bank details are now recorded for the December billing cycle.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So is this whole mess sorted out now or what?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have logged ticket reference BD-99104 for the billing dispute and applied the suspension hold, so the balance stands pending audit.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, it's not sorted at all! The wrongful charges are still sitting there, you haven't refunded my forty-eight pounds, and I've wasted forty minutes on the phone for nothing!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The audit team will contact you via email once their investigation concludes within seven days.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I am going to raise a formal complaint with the ombudsman if this isn't wiped off my account by Friday.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You have the right to register a formal complaint via our website at any time.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I definitely will be.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else regarding your S-Net services I can assist you with today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, I just want this nightmare over with.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net customer billing.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Goodbye.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net. Goodbye Declan.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Whatever.
